newsitem.title: USA: Burns and Roe to do tritium gas production project.
newsitem.headline: Burns and Roe to do tritium gas production project.

text.p: Burns and Roe Enterprises Inc. of New Jersey was selected to do a demonstration project to provide a new source of tritium, which is a gas used in nuclear weapons, the Energy Department said Thursday.

If the Energy Department eventually approves the project, the privately-owned company would get a nearly $3 billion federal contract through 2007 to build a plant at the department's Savannah River facility in South Carolina, the department said.

The Energy Department is to decide by October 1998 whether to produce tritium, a form of hydrogen, with a linear accelerator plant that makes the gas by capturing neutrons in helium, or with an existing light water nuclear reactor.
Burns and Roe, which designs and builds nuclear and coal power plants and hazardous waste treatment systems, would build the accelerator facility.

The lightwater reactor likely would be less expensive, but its use would involve fissile materials, production of nuclear waste, and a nuclear chain reaction which critics said could counter the nation's goals for nuclear non-proliferation.

Burns and Roe is to do the demonstration project at the department's Los Alamos National Laboratory in New Mexico, which is expected to cost beteen $5.5 million and $20 million in 1997, a Los Alamos spokesman said.
The United States has not produced tritium gas since 1988 and has relied on tritium from dismantled weapons to meet national security requirements, the Energy Department said.
But a new source will be needed by 2005-2007, it said.
